A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DualAnoDiff and support matching the methods, equations, experiments and results. All pages are readable, including v3's supplementary Sections 6–9. The supplied v1 ends with references.

before.justification: Tables 1–5 and accompanying figures report original MVTec generation, downstream inspection and ablation results.

after.justification: v3 retains original MVTec experiments and supplies additional quantitative ablations and generated-image comparisons in its supplement.

M1.justification: Both versions use two LoRA diffusion branches, nested prompts, SAIM, BCM and segmentation-based mask extraction. The later explanations and equation corrections clarify this existing procedure without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate anomaly generation, detection, localization and classification on MVTec AD. The supplementary examples and ablations use categories already covered by v1; no additional dataset or distinct test environment is evaluated.

E2.justification: The numerical comparator sets in Tables 1–4 remain unchanged. The expanded qualitative comparison in v3 Figure 7 adds Crop-Paste, DiffAug, CDC and SDGAN alongside the DefectGAN, DFMGAN and AnomalyDiffusion comparisons shown in v1 Figure 5.

E3.justification: The stated generation budget increases from 500 to 1,000 images or pairs per anomaly type for quality evaluation and downstream training. Classification prose changes from ResNet-34 to ResNet-18, resolving v1's disagreement with its Table 3 caption without proving an actual classifier change. The dataset split and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 provides a qualitative prompt comparison and a partial BCM ablation table. v3 Tables 6–7 supply category-level quantitative comparisons of category-name prompts, special-token prompts and BCM at both pixel and image levels. Figures 8–14 add detailed case studies of anomaly shape, location, realism and mask alignment.

E5.justification: v1 gives no repeated-run information. v3 Section 9.3 newly discloses training the downstream U-Net three times and selecting the best result. This does not establish an increase in runs, and neither version reports variability, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 updates the reported mean IS/IC-LPIPS from 1.90/0.37 to 1.93/0.38. Table 3 revises category scores and its reported classification average from 72.26 to 79.67. Differently reported experimental settings prevent treating these as same-setting gains. Tables 2, 4 and 5 retain their values, while supplementary Tables 6–7 and Figures 7–14 add substantial results.

T1.justification: Equation 5 corrects the key and value projections from W_Q to W_K and W_V. Equation 6 corrects the second expectation's encoded image from E(I) to E(Ia), consistent with the anomaly-part loss already described. These are limited mathematical corrections; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain dual-interrelated anomaly image/part generation, aligned masks, background compensation and improved downstream inspection. v3 explicitly mentions mask accuracy in the abstract, but this claim was already present in v1's contributions and conclusion.

C2.justification: v3 expands the explanation of object/background decoupling and prompt-prior mismatch. Section 7 adds the qualification that special-token prompts underperform for toothbrush without BCM. Figure 10 acknowledges background-color differences and claims they do not affect downstream detection, a qualification absent from v1.

D1.justification: v1 defers implementation details to supplementary material absent from that PDF. v3 Sections 6 and 9 supply training budgets, batch size, learning rate, LoRA rank, hardware, timings, augmentation, inference settings and explicit U2-Net mask extraction. A repository link is added, although the abstract still says code will be made available.

R1.justification: v3 expands citations to anomaly-inspection and few-shot methods, including SimpleNet, SoftPatch+ and FEditNet++, and adds references for FID, IS and DiffAug. It also explicitly distinguishes personalization methods by their lack of pixel annotations. The central positioning relative to DFMGAN and AnomalyDiffusion remains stable.

P1.justification: The title and author block change, sections become numbered, and local rewrites clarify prompts, SAIM and BCM. The main section order and much of the wording are retained; newly supplied material is organized into supplementary Sections 6–9.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 2, removes the anomaly-part panel from Figure 3, changes an example column in Figure 5 and reformats the main tables and layout. The supplement adds two substantial tables and eight figures, materially expanding the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility through concrete implementation details and strengthens component evidence with quantitative prompt ablations. It also resolves the classifier-description conflict, and Table 3's revised average agrees with its revised category rows. These gains are limited by reporting problems in the added evidence: Table 7 reports full-model AUROC/F1 averages of 99.8/99.8, whereas its category rows average approximately 98.17/97.10. Run variability also remains unquantified.
